summary:
Forgotten Explorers is a free, story-driven web app that teaches children aged 8 to 12 about the NASA robots left on the Moon, on Mars and in deep space. Visitors explore a 3D map, then open a robot’s page to see real NASA photos, a 3D model, mission facts with source links, and a clear status: Left Behind, Went Silent or Still Talking. In Last Message mode, each robot tells its final days in its own voice, with poetic lines clearly labeled as poetic. A quiz that brings back missed questions, and games with levels, help children remember what they learned.

It answers the challenge “Abandoned but not Forgotten” by giving silent machines a story, so children connect with the science they made possible. It matters because kids usually hear only about active missions. The app is built on NASA images, NASA 3D models and JPL data, and it works with a keyboard, captions and reduced motion.
details:
What it does
Forgotten Explorers is a free web app for ages 8 to 12 that tells the stories of NASA robots left on the Moon, Mars and in deep space. A 60-second “Start here” tour guides visitors with no login. On a 3D map, they open a robot’s page to see real NASA photos, a NASA 3D model, mission facts with source links, and a status: Left Behind, Went Silent or Still Talking. In Last Message mode, the robot tells its final days in its own voice, and poetic lines are labeled as poetic. A quiz that brings back missed questions, plus games with levels and XP, help children remember.

Impact and benefits
Children usually hear only about active missions. This app shows them the robots that went quiet and the science they made possible. It is free, works on phones and laptops, and supports keyboard use, captions and reduced motion.

Tools
Vite, vanilla JavaScript, Three.js, and a Node.js API with caching, rate limiting and tests. GitHub Actions and Lighthouse for quality checks. Data comes from the NASA Image and Video Library, NASA 3D Resources, JPL and NASA mission pages, and NASA Mars Trek path data. Distances show “live” or “saved snapshot”. AI tools used: Claude Code, Claude, ChatGPT and GitHub Copilot.

Creativity and considerations
Each robot speaks for itself, like a short film. We focused on accuracy (source links and “draft” labels), accessibility, child safety (no login, no ads), and honesty (no NASA logo, independent project).

Next steps
More abandoned robots with checked stories, teacher worksheets, more languages, and an offline classroom mode.
